# Exact mass asymptotics for the two-dimensional O(4) lattice model

Coordinate `EN-115-000-0020-2-2026-PR-T4-UK-EX-M2-B-PH-M-0406` | `PM-215.3` | status ACTIVE | original slug `Exact-mass-asymptotics-for-the-two-dimensional-O4-lattice-model-October-5-2026` | date 2026-10-05 | derived from the openai/math preprint Exact-mass-asymptotics-for-the-two-dimensional-O4-lattice-model-October-5-2026, modified (Apache-2.0). ```json
{
  "abstract_verbatim": "For the nearest-neighbor $`O(4)`$ model on the square lattice at inverse temperature <i>β</i>, we prove the exact low-temperature asymptotic\n\n$`\\displaystyle m_{\\mathrm{lat}}(\\beta)\\sim 32\\exp(\\pi/4-1/2)\\sqrt\\beta\\,\\exp(-\\pi\\beta) \\qquad (\\beta\\to\\infty).`$\n\nHere the mass is the gap of the full Osterwalder–Schrader transfer operator, including rotation-invariant local-observable sectors, in units of one original lattice time step.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> For the nearest-neighbor $`O(4)`$ model on the square lattice at inverse temperature <i>β</i>, we prove the exact low-temperature asymptotic
> 
> $`\displaystyle m_{\mathrm{lat}}(\beta)\sim 32\exp(\pi/4-1/2)\sqrt\beta\,\exp(-\pi\beta) \qquad (\beta\to\infty).`$
> 
> Here the mass is the gap of the full Osterwalder–Schrader transfer operator, including rotation-invariant local-observable sectors, in units of one original lattice time step.

- **claim-exact-lattice-mass** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-main)): For the measures <a href="#eq:gibbs" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:gibbs">[eq:gibbs]</a>, the full transfer gap <a href="#eq:mass-definition" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:mass-definition">[eq:mass-definition]</a> satisfies $$\label{eq:main-limit} \lim_{\beta\to\infty} \frac{\exp(\pi\beta)}{\sqrt\beta}\,m_{\mathrm{lat}}(\beta) =32\exp\!\left(\frac\pi4-\frac12\right).$$
  - Explanation: Determines the leading low-temperature mass prefactor for the full local-observable transfer space in the specified lattice normalization.
- **claim-rotator-association-signs** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-wilson-signs)): The $\alpha$ marginal in <a href="#eq:wilson-two-planes" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:wilson-two-planes">[eq:wilson-two-planes]</a> is associated. For two even-degree monomials each using a single spin component, the covariance is nonnegative when their components agree and nonpositive when they differ. The same signs hold for the two components of a zero-field ferromagnetic plane rotator.
  - Explanation: Association of the angular marginal controls the signs of covariances between even monomials using the same or different components.
- **claim-finite-graph-sector-comparison** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-wilson-covariance)): For the law <a href="#eq:wilson-graph-law" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:wilson-graph-law">[eq:wilson-graph-law]</a>, let $P,Q$ be spin monomials of positive degrees $r,s$ with site lists $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$, and put $$G=\max_{x\in\mathcal X,\ y\in\mathcal Y}\mathbb E_J(q_x^1q_y^1).$$ Then $G\ge0$, and a constant $C_{r,s}$ depending only on the degrees satisfies $$\|\operatorname{Cov}_J(P,Q)\|\le C_{r,s} \begin{cases} G^2,&r,s\ \text{even},\\ G,&r,s\ \text{odd},\\ 0,&r+s\ \text{odd}. \end{cases} \label{eq:sector-cov}$$ If either monomial is constant, its covariance is zero. The estimate is independent of the finite graph and its nonnegative couplings.
  - Explanation: Bounds monomial covariance by the appropriate parity-dependent power of the largest component correlation, uniformly in the finite ferromagnetic graph.
- **claim-spin-detects-full-gap** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-wilson-full-gap)): For every $\beta>0$, in the periodic plane state, $$m(\beta)=-\log r_*(\beta) =-\log\lim_{n\to\infty} \bigl(\mathbb E_{\mu_\beta}q_0^1q_{(n,0)}^1\bigr)^{1/n}. \label{eq:full-gap}$$ The transfer norm on the even subspace orthogonal to the vacuum is at most $r_*(\beta)^2$. Its gap is therefore at least $2m(\beta)$. The logarithms can be read in the extended sense; the imported upper bound below makes them finite throughout the large-$\beta$ regime.
  - Explanation: Identifies the full transfer gap through a component correlation and gives a stronger spectral bound for centered even observables.
- **claim-bounded-cylinder-detector** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-wilson-detector)): The restriction of $U_{\beta,\ell}$ to the centered even row subspace has norm at most $\tau_{\beta,\ell}^2$. There is a real row function $F$, with $\|F\|\le1$, odd under reflection of one spin component, such that $$\omega_{\beta,\ell}(F\,F\circ\vartheta_n) \ge\frac{\tau_{\beta,\ell}}{1+\tau_{\beta,\ell}}\, \tau_{\beta,\ell}^{\,n},\qquad n\ge0, \label{eq:wilson-detector-overlap}$$ where $\vartheta_n$ translates by $n$ rows.
  - Explanation: Constructs a bounded component-odd row observable with a controlled overlap on the first cylinder excitation.
- **claim-component-visibility** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-wilson-visibility)): For fixed $\beta>0$ there is a finite constant $C_\beta$, independent of even $\ell\ge4$, such that bounded row functions $F,G$ of modulus at most one, both odd under reflection of component one, satisfy $$\|\omega_{\beta,\ell}(F\,G\circ\vartheta_n)\| \le C_\beta\sum_{x\in R_0,\ y\in R_n} \omega_{\beta,\ell}(q_x^1q_y^1), \qquad n\ge1. \label{eq:wilson-visibility}$$ Here $R_0,R_n$ are the two rows of $\ell$ sites.
  - Explanation: Converts correlations of bounded component-odd row observables into a sum of component correlations with circumference-independent cost at fixed coupling.
- **claim-imported-wilson-trajectories** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-wilson-input)): For each $N\ge1$ and $h\in I_H$ there exists an admitted nearest-neighbor trajectory of depth $N$ ending at $h$. Every sufficiently large bare coupling occurs in at least one such trajectory. There are fixed integers $N_0,M_0>0$, with $M_0$ dyadic, such that every admitted trajectory with $N\ge N_0$, terminal coupling $h\in I_H$, bare coupling $\beta$, and spacing $a=L^{-N}$ obeys $$\begin{aligned} 4\log Z_\beta(M_0/a,M_0/a) -\log Z_\beta(2M_0/a,2M_0/a)&\le2^{-10}, \label{eq:wilson-seed}\\ m(\beta)/a&\le\log8, \label{eq:wilson-input-upper}\\ N\log L&=\pi\beta-\tfrac12\log\beta+O_{L,H}(1). \label{eq:wilson-calibration} \end{aligned}$$ In particular $a\asymp_{L,H}\sqrt\beta e^{-\pi\beta}$. The error bound and the two preceding inequalities are uniform over these trajectories. The periodic plane limit is unique and has a positive full OS gap for every fixed $\beta>0$.
  - Explanation: Supplies admitted trajectories, calibration, trace seeds, and full-gap input imported from the sharp-order analysis.
- **claim-uniform-cylinder-partition-rates** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-wilson-partition-rate)): For all admitted trajectories of Proposition <a href="#prop:wilson-input" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:wilson-input">7</a> with $N\ge N_0$ and terminal coupling $h\in I_H$, there are constants $C_H,w_H<\infty$, independent of the trajectory, such that every dyadic $w\ge w_H$ satisfies $$\left\|E(w)-\frac{m(\beta)}a\right\|\le C_Hw^{-1/4} \label{eq:wilson-cylinder-rate}$$ and $$\left\|-\frac{\log\Delta(w)}w-\frac{m(\beta)}a\right\| \le C_Hw^{-1/4}. \label{eq:partition-rate}$$
  - Explanation: Controls the approach of both cylinder energies and an area-canceling partition rate to the plane mass uniformly over admitted trajectories.
- **claim-long-rectangle-tail** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-wilson-long-rectangles)): Uniformly over admitted trajectories with $N\ge N_0$ and $h\in I_H$, for all sufficiently large dyadic $t$ and dyadic $w\ge2t$, $$p(t,w)\le C(w/t)e^{-ct}. \label{eq:wilson-long-rectangle}$$
  - Explanation: Extends square trace-tail control to long rectangles with a prefactor proportional to their aspect ratio.
- **claim-brownian-parity-asymptotic** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-brownian-parity)): Let $b\to\infty$, and suppose that for a fixed $D>0$ $$W\asymp e^{\pi b}b^{-1/2}(\log b)^D.$$ Suppose also that there is a fixed $C_*>0$ such that every particle number attaining either parity maximum satisfies $\|n_{\mathrm p}/W-b^2\|\le C_*b$. Then $$\log\tau_0-\log\tau_1 \sim32\sqrt2\,b^{1/2}e^{-\pi b}. \label{eq:B1}$$
  - Explanation: Determines the Brownian parity norm difference on the prescribed growing circles, conditional on localization of every maximizing particle sector.
- **claim-positive-contact-ground-state** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-brownian-ground)): For fixed $W>0$ and $n_{\mathrm p}\ge0$, the ground state of $H_c$ in every nonempty fixed-weight sector is simple for each $c>0$. In a fixed color sign convention it is strictly positive. The operator $H_2$ commutes with $T_{n_{\mathrm p}}$, and the norm of $T_{n_{\mathrm p}}$ is its eigenvalue on the balanced ground state of $H_2$. The commutation statement remains valid with corresponding diagonal boundary twists for the particle sections and the Brownian heat loop.
  - Explanation: Identifies the transfer norm with the transfer eigenvalue on a simple positive balanced ground state of the commuting contact Hamiltonian.
- **claim-endpoint-parametrization** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-brownian-equations)): For every $B>0$, the first equation in <a href="#eq:B3" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:B3">[eq:B3]</a> has a unique positive solution. There is a unique value $b=b(B)>\sqrt3$ for which the second has an even solution satisfying $\epsilon(B)=0$; this solution is positive inside $(-B,B)$ and negative outside. The function $b(B)$ is continuous and strictly increasing. If $\eta_B=-\epsilon'$ on $(-B,B)$, then $$(1-K*)\eta_B= \frac{2x}{x^2+1}+\frac{2x}{x^2+9},\qquad \|x\|<B,$$ and $$4\log b=\log9+\int_0^B a(x)\eta_B(x)\,dx, \qquad a(x)=\frac2\pi\arctan\frac4x. \label{eq:B4}$$ The inverse of $1-K*$ on $(-B,B)$ has supremum norm $O(1+B)$.
  - Explanation: Selects the coupling from the endpoint, establishes the dressed-energy sign change, and controls the interval resolvent.
- **claim-endpoint-density-mass-asymptotics** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-brownian-asymptotics)): As $B\to\infty$, with $b=b(B)$ and $m_*$ defined above, $$\begin{aligned} b(B)&=\frac B2+\frac{\log(4\pi B)+1}{\pi}+o(1),\\ m_*&\sim\frac{8}{\pi e\sqrt B}\,e^{-\pi B/2},\\ 2\int_{-B}^B\rho_B(x)\,dx &=\frac{B^2}{4}+\frac B\pi\log B+O(B). \end{aligned} \label{eq:B5}$$ There are positive constants $c_1,C_1$ such that, for all sufficiently large $B$, $\rho_B\ge c_1\sqrt B$ within distance one of either endpoint, and $\rho_B\le C_1B$ throughout the interval. For every $B>0$, the solution also satisfies $\sup_{y\in\mathbb R}\|\epsilon'(y)\|\le\pi/2$.
  - Explanation: Evaluates the endpoint correction, particle density, and exponentially small odd contribution while retaining its multiplicative constant.
- **claim-halfline-wiener-hopf-profile** (construction, [source](#stmt-brownian-halfline)): There are functions $U,V:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$, continuous from the right at zero and continuous on $(0,\infty)$, with the following properties. Extend $U$ by zero on $(-\infty,0)$. Then $$U(X)=(K_1*U)(X)\quad(X>0), \qquad V(Y)=(K_1*U)(-Y)\quad(Y\ge0),$$ and $U(X)>0$, $V(Y)>0$ for $X,Y\ge0$. For $\operatorname{Re}s>0$, $$\label{eq:B7} \begin{split} C(s)&=\frac{\sqrt{s}\, \exp\!\left\{\frac{s}{2\pi} \left(\log\frac{s}{2\pi}-1\right)\right\}} {\Gamma(1+s/(2\pi))},\\ \int_0^\infty e^{-sX}U(X)\,dX &=\frac{\sqrt\pi}{2sC(s)},\qquad \int_0^\infty e^{-sY}V(Y)\,dY =\frac{\sqrt\pi}{2s}C(s). \end{split}$$ The logarithm and square root in this formula are the principal branches. Moreover, $$\label{brownian:U-asymptotic} \begin{aligned} U(X)&=\sqrt X+ \frac{\log X+C'}{4\pi\sqrt X} +O\!\left(X^{-3/2}(1+\log^2X)\right),\\ C'&=\log(8\pi)+1,\qquad X\longrightarrow\infty, \end{aligned}$$ while $V(Y)=O((1+Y)^{-1/2})$ and $U(0)=V(0)=\sqrt\pi/2$.
  - Explanation: Constructs positive endpoint profiles through Laplace transforms and determines the correction required for matching the interval interior.
- **claim-uniform-endpoint-matching** (bound, [source](#stmt-brownian-uniform)): Let $h,w$ solve the scaled interval equations stated above, with $B=4/\delta$, and let $F_{j,h},F_{j,w}$ denote the two rows of <a href="#eq:B6" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:B6">[eq:B6]</a>. Define, on the real line away from the endpoints, $$\begin{aligned} h_{\mathrm{app}}(x) &=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(F_{0,h}(x)+\delta F_{1,h}(x)\bigr) +\sqrt{2\delta}\bigl[-D_0(X_+(x))+D_0(X_-(x))\bigr],\\ w_{\mathrm{app}}(x) &=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(F_{0,w}(x)+\delta F_{1,w}(x)\bigr) +\sqrt{2\delta}\bigl[D_0(X_+(x))+D_0(X_-(x))\bigr]. \end{aligned}$$ There exist constants $C<\infty$ and $\delta_0>0$ such that, for $0<\delta<\delta_0$, $$\\|h-h_{\mathrm{app}}\\|_{L^\infty(-1,1)} +\\|w-w_{\mathrm{app}}\\|_{L^\infty(-1,1)} \le C\delta^{3/2}\|\log\delta\|.$$ Both approximants have finite one-sided limits at the endpoints.
  - Explanation: Replaces singular outer expansions with exact endpoint profiles and controls their combined uniform error.
- **claim-algebraic-bethe-eigenvectors** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-bethe-algebra)): Suppose the momenta and auxiliary variables are nonsingular solutions of $$\label{eq:B8} \begin{aligned} e^{ik_j\mathcal W} &=e^{i\zeta+2i\chi} \prod_{t\ne j}\frac{k_j-k_t+2i}{k_j-k_t-2i} \left(\frac{Q_0(k_j-i)}{Q_0(k_j+i)}\right)^2, &&1\leq j\leq n_p,\\ e^{-2i\chi}\prod_{j=1}^{n_p} \frac{a_r-k_j-i}{a_r-k_j+i} &=\prod_{s\ne r}\frac{a_r-a_s-2i}{a_r-a_s+2i}, &&1\leq r\leq M. \end{aligned}$$ Here nonsingular means that the displayed rational functions and the coefficient formulas in the proof are defined by ordinary substitution. For each binary index, apply the upper-right entries $B(a_1),\ldots,B(a_M)$ of the spin-$\frac12$ monodromy defined below to the all-up vector. The tensor product of these two vectors, propagated by <a href="#eq:bethe-R" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:bethe-R">[eq:bethe-R]</a>, gives a periodic twisted eigenfunction of $H_2$ whenever it is nonzero. Its energy is $\sum_j k_j^2$.* *More generally, let $S_J$ be the spin-$J$ angular momentum matrices, $g_J$ the spin-$J$ representation of $g$, $\sigma$ the Pauli matrices, and $$\mathcal L_J(x)=x-2iS_J\cdot\sigma, \qquad F(u)=\prod_{j=1}^{n_p}(u-k_j).$$ In the product of $\mathcal L_J(u-k_j)$, put later physical sites on the left. Its auxiliary trace with twist $g_J^{-1}$ has eigenvalue $$\label{eq:B9} t_J(u)=\sum_{m=-J}^{J}e^{-2im\chi}F(u-2im) \frac{Q_0(u-i(2J+1))Q_0(u+i(2J+1))} {Q_0(u-i(2m+1))Q_0(u-i(2m-1))}.$$ All these identities continue meromorphically in the variables. A nonzero continuation limit of the plane eigenfunction is again an eigenfunction at the limiting parameters.
  - Explanation: Constructs twisted contact eigenfunctions and auxiliary trace eigenvalues from nonsingular Bethe solutions, with meromorphic continuation to nonzero limits.
- **claim-line-spectral-resolution** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-bethe-line)): For every fixed integer $n_p=2M+\ell\geq0$, every $c>0$, and every $s>0$, the heat kernel of $H_c$ on the ordered line chamber is $$\begin{split} e^{-sH_c}(X,Y) ={}&\sum_{\ell'+2m'=n_p} \frac{(2c)^{m'}}{\ell'!\,m'!} \int_{\mathbb R^{\ell'+m'}} E_X^{\ell'm'}(k,u)E_Y^{\ell'm'}(k,u)^\dagger\\ &\quad{}\times \exp\left\{-s\left( \sum_{a=1}^{\ell'}k_a^2+ 2\sum_{a=1}^{m'}u_a^2-\frac{m'c^2}{2} \right)\right\} \prod_{a=1}^{\ell'}\frac{dk_a}{2\pi} \prod_{a=1}^{m'}\frac{du_a}{2\pi}. \end{split} \label{eq:B10}$$ Empty products and the vacuum term have their usual value $1$. The transform defined by the kernels in <a href="#eq:B10" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:B10">[eq:B10]</a>, with the square roots of the displayed weights, is an isometry. Moreover, $H_c+Mc^2/2\geq0$, and its quadratic form is the integral of $$\sum_{a=1}^{\ell'}k_a^2+ 2\sum_{a=1}^{m'}u_a^2+\frac{(M-m')c^2}{2}$$ against the squared modulus of this transform.
  - Explanation: Resolves the line heat kernel into singles and singlet pairs and gives an isometric transform with a nonnegative shifted energy form.
- **claim-shuffle-span-decay** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-bethe-shuffle-decay)): At fixed $n_p$, there are constants $C_{n_p}<\infty$ and $a_{n_p}>0$, independent of $c>0$ and the real momenta, such that every group just defined satisfies $$\bigl\\|E_{X,\mathfrak g}^{\ell'm'}(k,u)\bigr\\| \leq C_{n_p} \exp\left\{-a_{n_p}c \sum_{\text{components }\mathcal I} \bigl(X_{\max\mathcal I}-X_{\min\mathcal I}\bigr)\right\}. \label{eq:B11}$$ The norm is the operator norm after summing the shuffles in the group.
  - Explanation: Bounds grouped shuffle waves by exponential decay in their component spans after cancellations at coincident pair centers.
- **claim-pair-chart-compactness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-bethe-pair-compactness)): Fix $W_0>0$, $n_p=2M+\ell$, and $C<\infty$. Let $c_j\to\infty$ and let $\psi_j$ be normalized vectors in the form domain of the circle Hamiltonian such that $$\left\langle\psi_j, (H_{c_j}+Mc_j^2/2)\psi_j\right\rangle\leq C.$$ After passage to a subsequence, the localized functions in the pair coordinates just defined converge in $L^2$ on every fixed retained chart. For each seam and pair assignment these limits are compatible under enlargement of the chart and have the form $$f_{\alpha,\mathfrak p}(q,v)\, \exp\left\{-\frac12\sum_{a=1}^M z_a\right\} \bigotimes_{a=1}^M (s_a^L\otimes s_a^R). \label{eq:B12}$$ Here $v$ and its color are present only if $\ell=1$; the coefficient $f_{\alpha,\mathfrak p}$ includes that color. As $\delta\downarrow0$ and $Z\uparrow\infty$, the sum of the squared norms of these chart limits tends to $1$, counted with the fixed square partition of unity. There is no norm lost away from the pair coincidence manifolds or at their intersections. Inner products of two sequences converging in this sense converge to the corresponding sums of inner products of their limits.
  - Explanation: Obtains subsequential strong convergence on separated pair charts and proves that their exhaustion retains the full norm and inner products.
- **claim-ground-test-positive-overlap** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-cor-bethe-ground-test)): Fix a circle length $W_0>0$ and a particle number $n_p=2M+\ell$, with $\ell\in\{0,1\}$, and work in the fixed-weight sector balanced in each binary index. Suppose a normalized eigenbranch has energy $-Mc^2/2+O(1)$ as $c\to\infty$. Suppose also that, after one common phase choice for all charts, every subsequential limit in the pair charts has the form <a href="#eq:B12" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:B12">[eq:B12]</a>. Require its scalar center coefficient to be strictly positive almost everywhere that the limiting chart cutoff is positive, in the static-sign convention of Lemma <a href="#lem:brownian-ground" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:brownian-ground">11</a>; when $\ell=1$, the remaining single has the majority color in each index. Then the branch is the ground state for all sufficiently large $c$.
  - Explanation: Identifies a strong-coupling eigenbranch as the ground state by positive limiting overlap, without requiring completeness of periodic Bethe states.
- **claim-pair-center-counting-jacobian** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-bethe-centers)): Under the parameter assumptions at the start of this Section, for every $\mathcal W\geq W$, <a href="#eq:B13" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:B13">[eq:B13]</a> has a reflection-symmetric solution with $v=0$ and $u_1<\cdots<u_M$. With $v$ fixed, the pair solution is unique. Define $$Z_c(x)=\frac{x}{\pi} +\frac{1}{\pi\mathcal W}\sum_{j=1}^M \arctan\frac{x-u_j}{4} -\frac{\ell}{2\pi\mathcal W}\varphi(x), \qquad d(x)=Z_c'(x).$$ Then $Z_c$ is odd and $$d(x)=\frac1\pi+\frac1{\mathcal W}\sum_jK(x-u_j) -\frac\ell{\mathcal W}(K_1-K_3)(x), \qquad Z_c(u_j)=\frac{j-(M+1)/2}{\mathcal W}.$$ Let $B_c>0$ be determined by $Z_c(B_c)=M/(2\mathcal W)$. The following bounds hold uniformly:* 1. *$d$ is bounded below by a positive constant; $B_c=O((1+b)^2)$; $d$ and any fixed number of its derivatives are bounded by $\operatorname{poly}(b)$. Neighboring centers have separation at least $1/(\mathcal W\operatorname{poly}(b))$.* 2. *On $(-B_c,B_c)$, $$\label{eq:B14} d=\rho_{B_c} -\frac\ell{\mathcal W}(1-K*)_{B_c}^{-1}(K_1-K_3) +O\!\left(\frac{\operatorname{poly}(b)}{\mathcal W^2}\right).$$ The inverse function in the middle term has bounded supremum and $L^1$ norm, independently of $B_c$.* 3. *$B_c\leq B_*+O(1)$. At $\mathcal W=W$ one also has $B_c\geq B_*-O(1)$.* 4. *The full Jacobian of <a href="#eq:B13" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:B13">[eq:B13]</a>, including the single equation when present, is invertible. Its inverse has row sums bounded by a fixed power of $\mathcal W$.
  - Explanation: Constructs ordered symmetric centers, approximates their counting density, and controls the full Jacobian including the weak single-particle direction.
- **claim-pair-spacing-suppression** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-bethe-suppression)): Let the centers be those of Lemma <a href="#lem:bethe-centers" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:bethe-centers">21</a>. Set $$A(x)=\log\frac{\|x\|\sqrt{x^2+16}}{x^2+4}, \qquad \kappa(x)=1+(A*\rho_{B_c})(x).$$ Uniformly for $\mathcal W\geq W$, $$\label{eq:B16} \inf_{\|x\|\leq B_c}\mathcal W\kappa(x) \geq c_2\mathcal W\sqrt{1+B_c}\,e^{-\pi B_c/2} \gg\log\mathcal W,$$ where the last ratio tends to infinity as $b\to\infty$. Moreover, $$\mathcal W+\sum_{t\ne j}A(u_j-u_t) =\mathcal W\kappa(u_j)+O(\log\mathcal W)$$ uniformly in $j$.
  - Explanation: Shows that the external pair products suppress spacing corrections strongly enough to overcome polynomial losses along the circumference ray.
- **claim-finite-circle-root-continuation** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-bethe-roots)): For the parameter range of this Section, the center solution of <a href="#eq:B13" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:B13">[eq:B13]</a> has a locally unique continuation to solutions of <a href="#eq:B8" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:B8">[eq:B8]</a>, with the singular solutions understood as analytic continuation limits. At zero twist write these solutions as $$k_{j+}=a_j+i+X_j,\qquad k_{j-}=a_j-i+Y_j, \qquad u_j^{\mathrm{true}}=(k_{j+}+k_{j-})/2.$$ For every fixed $A_0>0$, the differences between the true variables and their formal center values are $O_{A_0}(\mathcal W^{-A_0})$, uniformly for $\mathcal W\geq W$, once $b$ is sufficiently large. The solutions are locally analytic in $\mathcal W$ and in twists near zero, and these local solutions link along $[W,\infty)$. At fixed $n_p$, their zero-twist centers satisfy $$\label{eq:B18} u_j=\frac{\pi(j-(M+1)/2)}{\mathcal W} +O_{n_p}(\mathcal W^{-2}) \qquad (\mathcal W\to\infty).$$ Ordinary nonsingular parameters form a generic set on this continued branch. A common twist translates every rapidity by $\zeta/\mathcal W$.
  - Explanation: Continues formal centers to true roots with superpolynomially small corrections and links the local analytic branches along the circumference ray.
- **claim-bethe-branch-ground-identification** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-bethe-ground)): At zero twist, the continuation-limit plane wave associated with Lemma <a href="#lem:bethe-roots" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:bethe-roots">23</a> has energy equal to the balanced ground energy of $H_2$ on the circle of circumference $W$. At generic parameters the plane wave is nonzero; at exceptional parameters the energy and eigenstate are understood by continuation. Thus its transfer eigenvalue is $\\|T_{n_p}\\|$. Infinitesimal twisted eigenvalues near this simple ground level may be used in its computation.
  - Explanation: Identifies the constructed branch with the simple balanced ground level and hence with the transfer norm, including exceptional parameters by continuation.
- **claim-finite-circle-transfer-formula** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-bethe-transfer-formula)): For the root branch of Lemma <a href="#lem:bethe-roots" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:bethe-roots">23</a>, with fixed finite $n_p$ and $W$, let $k_t$ be its momenta and let $t_j$ be the auxiliary trace eigenvalue in <a href="#eq:B9" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:B9">[eq:B9]</a>. The function $\Lambda_{n_p}(\zeta,\chi)$ is given near zero twist by $$\Lambda_{n_p}(\zeta,\chi) =\lambda^{n_p}\sum_{q,j}e^{-WE_{qj}+i\zeta q} \frac{(-2)^{n_p}i^{-2n_p}t_j(-iq)^2} {\displaystyle\prod_{t=1}^{n_p} \bigl[(d_j+1)^2-(ik_t-q)^2\bigr] \bigl[(d_j-1)^2-(ik_t-q)^2\bigr]} . \label{eq:B20}$$ The sum is over the admissible rotor sectors just specified. Apparent singularities in this expression are interpreted by analytic continuation from parameters at which coefficient extraction and the Bethe vectors are nonsingular.
  - Explanation: Computes the transfer scalar as the full rotor-sector sum, retaining winding contributions absent from a line calculation.
- **claim-uniform-transfer-rotor-suppression** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-bethe-transfer-uniform)): Fix $A,D>0$ and positive constants $c_-,c_+$. Suppose $b\to\infty$, $$c_-e^{\pi b}b^{-1/2}(\log b)^D \le W\le c_+e^{\pi b}b^{-1/2}(\log b)^D, \qquad \|n_p/W-b^2\|\le Ab.$$ There is $c'>0$, depending only on these fixed constants, such that at zero twist the sum in <a href="#eq:B20" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:B20">[eq:B20]</a> over $(q,j)\ne(0,0)$, divided by $Z_{n_p}(0,0)$, is $O(e^{-c'W})$, uniformly over these particle numbers. If $u_r$ are the real centers of <a href="#eq:B13" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:B13">[eq:B13]</a> at $\mathcal W=W$, then $$\log\\|T_{n_p}\\| =\sum_{r=1}^M p(u_r)+\ell f(0)+o(W^{-1}), \label{eq:B21}$$ with the error uniform over the same band.
  - Explanation: Suppresses nontrivial rotor sectors uniformly in the growing particle band and reduces the transfer logarithm to the formal-center sum.
- **claim-parity-variational-quadrature** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-bethe-parity-error)): Under the parameter assumptions of Lemma <a href="#lem:bethe-transfer-uniform" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:bethe-transfer-uniform">26</a>, the bracket in <a href="#eq:B22" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:B22">[eq:B22]</a> is at most $C/W$, uniformly in the particle band. In each parity there is a particle number in a band of the same form for which the bracket is at least $-C/W$. Specifically, one may take $M$ to be a nearest integer to $W\int\rho_{B_*}$ and set $n_p=2M+\ell$.
  - Explanation: Controls the variational quadrature bracket from above throughout the particle band and constructs near-optimal particle counts in both parities.
- **claim-regulator-partition-comparison** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-rg-comparison)): For all sufficiently large $\beta$ there are $$b=\beta+O(1),\qquad r=1+O(\beta^{-1}),\qquad c_x,c_t=\beta+O(1),\qquad \phi\in\mathbb R,$$ and a bulk volume scalar for each regulator, independent of the periods and of the time seam, with the following property. Remove these scalars from the partition functions. For dyadic lengths $$m_x\asymp\beta(\log\beta)^2, \qquad m_t\asymp\sqrt\beta(\log\beta)^4,$$ and also with $m_t$ replaced by $2m_t$, the Brownian regulator of heat time $r/b$ per fine horizontal cell, hence circumference $W=(r/b)L^Nm_x$, satisfies $$Z^B_\pm=Z^{F(\phi)}_\pm+ O(e^{-c\beta})Z^{F(0)}_+ . \label{eq:R1}$$ Here $c>0$ and the implicit constants are independent of $\beta$ and these periods. The same scalar for a given regulator is used for both seams and both temporal lengths.
  - Explanation: Matches scalar-stripped Brownian and augmented Wilson partitions on growing rectangles with an absolute error small enough to resolve the odd trace.
- **claim-free-block-operators** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-rg-free)): For either initial precision and either admissible shape, the free block iteration has uniformly elliptic, exponentially localized precisions $K_h$, conditional means $\mathsf P_h$, conditional covariances $C_h$, and positive edge stacks. Their required fixed derivatives, including shape derivatives, obey bounds on one common complex momentum neighborhood. For two initial precisions with the same shape, their histories differ by $CL^{-h}$ in those bounds. Constants needed to choose $L$ are independent of sufficiently large $L$.* *For a Brownian strip the edge lift consists of the horizontal term $l^{-1}$ and a positive matrix on the two endpoint values of each vertical edge. If $z$ is the vertical edge Laplacian symbol, this matrix is $$B_l(z)=l\sum_{m\ge1}J_m^* \bigl(1+l^2z/(\pi m)^2\bigr)^{-1}J_m, \qquad J_s(c,c')=(1-s)c+sc', \label{eq:R3}$$ where $J_m$ is the $m$th normalized sine coefficient of $J_s$. It is analytic near $[0,4]$, with uniform positive lower and upper bounds on that real interval. The formula holds also for cut vertical arrays, using their existing bonds. The affine precision, after strips are summed, is $\operatorname{diag}(l^{-1},l)$.
  - Explanation: Controls both free histories through localized elliptic block operators and positive edge lifts with a decaying history discrepancy.
- **claim-observation-displacement-phase** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-rg-observation)): For neighboring blocks $Y,Y'$ and their coarse edge $E$, $$r'_E\le\frac C L\sum_{e\subset Y\cup Y'}r_e +C\bigl(\|\eta_Y\|+\|\eta_{Y'}\|\bigr), \label{eq:R8}$$ where $\eta$ denotes the observation displacement, with its real coordinate measured before reduction. The constant is independent of large $L$ and of $R_j$. In conditional integration at fixed outputs and output integers, the old phase propagates to $\theta'=\theta LT$. Its remaining ratio is a product of local modulus-one factors depending only on sheet integers. Every nonidentity factor requires curvature in a block or an adjacent block pair.
  - Explanation: Controls quotient observation displacement and proves that phase defects require local integer curvature.
- **claim-exact-rg-step-comparison** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-rg-step)): Choose the constants in the order specified at the end of this section. For every sufficiently large $H$, every admitted layer $j\ge1$, every admitted rectangle or bulk density of Definition <a href="#def:rg-retained-class" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:rg-retained-class">30</a>, and either seam, the normalized block observation of Lemma <a href="#lem:rg-observation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:rg-observation">31</a> has an exact output in the same class, provided the output kinetic coefficients remain in the next admitted bands. In input normalization for the $w$ coefficients, each of the four kinetic coefficients changes by $$\alpha+\kappa/B+O_L(H_j^{-1.05}), \label{eq:R6}$$ where the direction and field indices are understood. The bounded coefficients $\alpha,\kappa$ and the next polynomial coefficients are given by the full-kernel Taylor map constructed below.* *For a Brownian input and a flat reference input on common lists, their outputs satisfy, for fixed $q_*<1$ and $c>0$, $$\begin{split} U'&\le q_*U+C_LL^{-h}+C_LH_j^{-c}\|\lambda\|,\\ \|\lambda'-\lambda\|&\le C_LU+C_LL^{-h} +C_LH_j^{-c}\|\lambda\|. \end{split} \label{eq:R7}$$ The coefficients in $\lambda'$ use output units, so the second estimate includes the real-coordinate conversion by $T$. No discrepancy of the old phase parameter is required. The restricted curvature cap renews with $$F_{h+1}=F_h+c_L\sqrt\beta\,p_j. \label{eq:R10}$$ Per output site, after the incoming scalar has been propagated, the scalar increment is $$4(L^2-1)\log g+V_L(l_q,l_w,\chi,T,h)+O_L(H_j^{-1}), \label{eq:R11}$$ where $V_L$ is real, uniformly bounded and Lipschitz on the admitted bands. Its arguments may also specify the type of free history. There is no additional power of $P_j$.
  - Explanation: Closes the retained class under exact observation, contracts paired local discrepancies, and records kinetic, curvature, and scalar updates.
- **claim-flag-curvature-energy-reserve** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-rg-reserve)): After the affine Gaussian squares have been selected and subtracted, each core with $s_c$ seeds retains energy at least $c_Lt^2s_c$, as in (**SharpO4?**, Lemma “Core reserve”), and, in addition, an unspent fixed fraction of $$ct\sum_{\text{input flags}}r_e +ct'\sum_{\text{output flags}}r'_E +c\sum_{\text{noise seeds}}\|\eta_Y\|^2. \label{eq:R9}$$ The energy is multiplied by $B$ in the density. The estimate holds on the retained tests and on the closed supports of the profile derivatives used below. If the core contains curvature it retains at least $c tP_j$ before multiplication by $B$.
  - Explanation: Preserves seed, flag, noise, and curvature energy after subtracting affine Gaussian squares, including on derivative supports.
- **claim-joint-prepared-factor-integration** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-rg-joint)): Fix a primary pattern and the complete-support convention above. Form local factors from: nonlinear rows minus their affine squares; stationary squares; old polynomial and regular-error terms; exceptional numerical defects; determinant and Gaussian-ratio chains; Haar Jacobian ratios; opened default-profile failures; and old covering weights. Include the compulsory cores and their frozen integrations.* *Suppose their ordinary smooth factors have envelopes $C_Lg^r\operatorname{poly}(M_j,p_j,s)$ of positive order $r$; ratio exponents have bounds $$\|Q_\alpha(Z)\|\le e_\alpha \left(1+\sum_{x\in I_\alpha}\|Z_x\|^2\right);$$ their eighth-root support-hit sums are sufficiently small; and every selection of $n$ distinct failure tests has simultaneous probability at most $\exp(-c_Lp_j^2n/M_j^D)$. Suppose further that the frozen integral of each core satisfies $$\int\|B_c\|\le\exp\{-c_Lp_j^2s_c+ C_LM_j^D(1+\|\log g\|)s_c\}$$ uniformly in the Gaussian arguments, while retaining the output-flag and curvature reserves. Here $B_c$ is the core integrand; its integral includes the frozen quaternion and real variables and the residual integer and tag sums, with Gaussian and output arguments held fixed. Suppose also that differentiation through hard dependencies can be represented by one simultaneous transport whose fixed-order $L^4$ scores cost a polynomial in total load and a fixed power of $g^{-1}$. Whenever such a negative power occurs, retain a core, failure, or exponentially accurate factor to pay it. Assume explicitly that every allowed differentiated product is a sum of polynomially many terms retaining the ordinary and ratio envelopes and the closed failure supports, apart from these score factors; a marked discrepancy uses its replacement envelope.* *Then every finite selection has a joint integral bound equal to the product of its stated majorants times a fixed polynomial in total load. This holds through eight normalized output derivatives for empty output inventory, and through seven derivatives for one marked input or parameter discrepancy. With nonempty output inventory it gives the sup norm and the corresponding discrepancy bound. A core with $s_c$ seeds retains $e^{-c_Lp_j^2s_c}$ after fixed losses, and each failure test retains $e^{-c_Lp_j^2/M_j^D}$; ratio chains may use their eighth-root envelopes. Disjoint complete supports factor exactly; overlapping factors require no independence.
  - Explanation: Turns simultaneous factor envelopes, tail estimates, transport scores, and core reserves into joint product bounds without assuming independence of overlapping factors.
- **claim-canonical-map-contraction** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-rg-canonical)): The principal Taylor map through normalized order four produces exactly the slots <a href="#eq:R5" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:R5">[eq:R5]</a>, scalar terms, an imaginary temporal linear $w$ term, and the four affine kinetic corrections in <a href="#eq:R6" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:R6">[eq:R6]</a>. At their own order and displayed prefactor, the diagonal response of a degree-$n\ge3$ slot has norm at most $CL^{2-n}$; a compensated quadratic has norm at most $C/L$. The constants are independent of $L$ before it is chosen. The map is triangular in the order <a href="#eq:R5" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:R5">[eq:R5]</a>, and its paired coefficient differences obey a strict contraction plus $C_L(L^{-h}+\|\lambda\|/H_j)$.
  - Explanation: Classifies the finite Taylor outputs and obtains diagonal contraction from prediction gains and affine compensation.
- **claim-exact-initial-retained-densities** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-init-density)): For the parameter choices of Theorem <a href="#thm:rg-step" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:rg-step">32</a>, the flat Wilson reference and the Brownian strip integral have exact representations in the retained class at scale $N$, on every admitted rectangle and with either time seam. The Wilson reference starts with zero canonical and regular-error lists and with flat covering labels. The Brownian representation starts from the uncorrected affine couplings $$(B_x^q,B_t^q)=b(r^{-1},r),\qquad (B_x^w,B_t^w)=bR^{-2}(r^{-1},r).$$ Its actual affine couplings differ from these by at most $C_L$. Their corrections, and its initial canonical coefficients, are given by the finite Taylor calculation through normalized order four, with coupling error $O_L(H_N^{-1.05})$. Its canonical caps can be fixed before choosing $P_0$ and $H$. All assertions include the normalized derivatives and period prescriptions of the retained class. The scalar extracted per initial site is the quantity in <a href="#eq:R14" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:R14">[eq:R14]</a> below.
  - Explanation: Places the flat reference and integrated Brownian strips in the same initial retained class while preserving finite Taylor coefficients and scalar normalization.
- **claim-brownian-path-endpoint-estimates** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-init-path-estimates)): The quantity <a href="#eq:init-rough-size" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:init-rough-size">[eq:init-rough-size]</a> controls a $\nu$-Hölder rough-path norm, and $$\Pr\{\mathcal N>D\}\le C e^{-cD^2}.$$ The same bound holds for a Gaussian bridge. Adding a path with bounded first derivative, or applying a smooth deterministic orthogonal rotation to the driving increments, preserves these estimates with the corresponding deterministic norm costs. Every fixed derivative of a smooth profile under these transformations has a polynomial bound in those norms and $\mathcal N$.* *For fixed endpoint sheets, let $K$ denote the unnormalized conditional row measure. Its total density obeys $$\begin{aligned} K(1)&\le Cg^{-4}\exp(-cg^{-2}r_{e_x}^2), \label{eq:init-heat-bound}\\ K(1_{\{\mathcal N>D\}})&\le Cg^{-4}e^{-cD^2}, \label{eq:init-conditioned-tail} \end{aligned}$$ uniformly in the endpoints. The versions of these bounds needed for smooth profile and path factors admit the fixed endpoint derivatives of the retained norm. Derivatives cost fixed polynomials in $g^{-1},\mathcal N,M,p$ and leave a positive fraction of the exponential reserves.
  - Explanation: Controls Brownian rough sizes and conditional heat densities, retaining Gaussian reserves after the endpoint derivatives needed for initialization.
- **claim-profile-endpoint-disintegration** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-init-endpoint)): On the profile $\zeta_s$, and for endpoints through the chart extension, the endpoint equation has the unique small solution $$A=A(D,gZ)=D+\text{terms of total degree at least two}.$$ Its coefficients and its fixed normalized derivatives satisfy the analytic path bounds of Lemma <a href="#lem:init-path-estimates" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:init-path-estimates">37</a>. With respect to bridge Gaussian measure, the conditional row density is the profile with this solution substituted, multiplied by $$C_g e^{-\|D\|^2/(2rg^2)} \exp\!\left\{-\frac{\|A\|^2-\|D\|^2}{2rg^2}\right\} \frac{J(0)}{J(D_q)}\det(\partial_D A). \label{eq:R12}$$ Here $J$ is the Haar Jacobian in quaternion logarithm coordinates, and $C_g$ is $g^{-4}$ times a smooth positive function of $r$ and $R$.
  - Explanation: Inverts the endpoint map on the small-path profile and gives the conditional density with its Gaussian, Haar, and inverse-map Jacobian factors.
- **claim-uniform-strip-gaussian-completion** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-init-completion)): For a finite periodic regular-row array or an array with arbitrary deleted rows, the Gaussian completion of <a href="#eq:R13" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:R13">[eq:R13]</a> admits finite-range numerical means and covariances. The covariances have uniform positive upper and lower bounds. The means and covariance deviations from the identity have exponential position bounds and summable estimates over bridge modes. Their exact Gaussian ratio factors satisfy the joint moment and support estimates used in Lemma <a href="#lem:rg-joint" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:rg-joint">34</a>. The stationary energy is the strip energy <a href="#eq:R3" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:R3">[eq:R3]</a>, up to local errors $C\operatorname{poly}(M,p)e^{-c_LM}$ in chart norms. These assertions are uniform in array length and in the deletion pattern.
  - Explanation: Completes the strip Gaussian with finite-range numerical laws and exact ratio factors whose bounds do not depend on array length or holes.
- **claim-initial-compulsory-reserve** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-init-reserve)): Choose $c_0,d_0$ sufficiently small, then the no-flag radius $D_0$ sufficiently large, and finally the path-profile constant $D_s$ sufficiently large. These choices precede the choice of $L$. For every fresh compulsory component, using the bounded-load record specified below and denoting its load by $s_c$, its integrated factor has the bound $$\exp\{-cp^2s_c+C_LM^D(1+\|\log g\|)s_c\},$$ or a stronger bound, with a positive reserve in the flagged increments. The bound is conditional on all regular-row Gaussian arguments read by the factor and holds on the differentiated profile supports as well. It also holds on the no-flag extensions used for empty-output factors.
  - Explanation: Pays for deleted paths, endpoint flags, and extracted rows with a conditional compulsory-factor reserve using a bounded-load record.
- **claim-reference-affine-continuity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-cmp-continuity)): On the flat reference, the quaternion affine couplings are exactly those of the nearest-neighbor evolution in (**SharpO4?**), and the physical circle affine stiffnesses, expressed in the original $v$ coordinate, do not change under blocking. At fixed $H,N$ and fixed scale factors $R_j$, all four displayed couplings of either evolution are continuous functions of the initial parameters along every strictly admitted finite segment.
  - Explanation: Identifies intrinsic reference couplings, preserves physical circle stiffness under blocking, and establishes continuity along strictly admitted segments.
- **claim-matched-trajectories-exist** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-cmp-shooting)): For every sufficiently large $\beta$ and the depth just specified, there are parameters $$b=\beta+O_L(1),\qquad r=1+O_L(\beta^{-1}),\qquad c_x,c_t=\beta+O_L(1)$$ for which both evolutions are admitted through layer zero and, with the distances of <a href="#eq:R7" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:R7">[eq:R7]</a>, $$\|\lambda_j\|+U_j\le C_L\rho^{N-j},\qquad \lambda_0=0, \qquad \max(q_*,L^{-1})<\rho<1. \label{eq:R15}$$ The constants are independent of $\beta$ and of the admitted periods.
  - Explanation: Obtains matched terminal affine coefficients and geometric control of the paired trajectories through a topological shooting argument.
- **claim-selected-row-exponential-moments** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-comparison-row-moments)): For a sufficiently large dyadic integer $B_T$ comparable to a fixed power of $\log H$, suppose the two periods are multiples of $2B_T$. There exists $0<\vartheta<1$ such that, for every set $I$ of unoriented rows and either time seam, $$\frac{1}{Z_{F,+}^{\rm end}} \int_{\mathcal F}e^{X_F^\eta}\Xi_F^\eta \exp\left(\vartheta\sum_{e\in I}Y_e\right)d\nu \le \exp(C_L\|I\|B_T^2\log H). \label{eq:R16}$$ The choices may make $1-\vartheta$ smaller than any prescribed fixed inverse power of $\log H$.
  - Explanation: Uses reflection positivity and translated tile estimates to control selected kinetic-row exponential moments for either time seam.
- **claim-flat-rough-region-replacements** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-comparison-flat-edits)): The constants $\varepsilon>0$ and $C$ can be fixed, in that order, so that the following holds for every sufficiently large $H$ and every admitted rectangle with both periods sufficiently large depending on $H$. For every flat configuration and every selected family of its regions $E_C$, there is a measurable probability distribution of flat replacement configurations that leaves all other sites unchanged, changes only integers incident on replaced sites, removes exactly the inventories of the selected regions, and creates no flagged bond.* *If $E$ is the union of the selected regions and $n=\|E\|$, there is a set $I_E$ of rows, containing every changed kinetic stencil, such that $\|I_E\|\le C d^2n$. For the original configuration $z$ and every sampled replacement $z'$, $$\sum_{e\in I_E}Y_e(z)\ge cp_0^2n/d^2, \qquad \sum_{e\in I_E}Y_e(z')\le C_Ld^2p_0^2n. \label{eq:comparison-edit-energy}$$ Relative to the site and incident-integer measure, the conditional fill density is at most $e^{C_Ln\log H}$ when $E\ne\Lambda$, and at most $P^{-1}e^{C_Ln\log H}$ when $E=\Lambda$. Nonempty exterior data retain their original winding. In a whole-torus replacement one may choose the winding, while keeping the prescribed time seam.
  - Explanation: Replaces selected rough regions while preserving flatness, controlling fill densities, and removing precisely their original inventories without an aspect-ratio loss.
- **claim-integrated-specified-edit-gain** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-comparison-edit-gain)): Fix the exact site sets of a selected family of original regions, let their union be $E$, and let $n=\|E\|$. Let $\mathcal Q$ be any measurable set of original flat configurations whose region construction gives those sets, with any further inventory restrictions imposed before sampling. Average the fillings of Lemma <a href="#lem:comparison-flat-edits" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:comparison-flat-edits">44</a>, keeping the original geometry fixed, and denote the filled configuration by $z'$. Then, for either time seam, $$\frac1{Z_{F,+}^{\rm end}}\int_{\mathcal Q}e^{X_F^\eta(z)} \mathbb E_{\rm fill\mid z}[\Xi_F^\eta(z')]\,d\nu(z) \le \exp(-c'p_0^2n/d^2). \label{eq:comparison-edit-gain}$$ This is the analogue of (**O3Continuum?**, Equation (7.15)).
  - Explanation: Converts a specified replacement into an integrated energy gain while keeping its original geometry fixed during sampling.
- **claim-flat-integrated-covering-comparison** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-comparison-flat-integrated)): Fix a constant multiplier of the retained covering cap. For sufficiently large $H$, let $e^{X_F^\eta}\Xi_F^\eta$ be the terminal flat-reference density constructed above, on any admitted dyadic rectangle whose periods exceed the stated $H$-dependent constant. Let $\widetilde\Xi^\eta$ be another mandatory covering sum with the same inventory conventions and complete supports, allowing complex weights. Use a common label list, setting absent weights equal to zero, and define $$d_\ell=\\|\widetilde\kappa_\ell-\kappa_{\ell,F}\\|_\infty, \qquad b_\ell=\\|\widetilde\kappa_\ell\\|_\infty+ \\|\kappa_{\ell,F}\\|_\infty.$$ Suppose $$\sup_x\sum_{\ell:x\in P_\ell}e^{64s_\ell}b_\ell \le C\exp(-p_0^{1/4}),$$ with the fixed multiplier $C$, and with the support and load bounds of the retained class. Then, for either $\eta$, $$\frac{\displaystyle\int_{\mathcal F}e^{X_F^\eta} \|\widetilde\Xi^\eta-\Xi_F^\eta\|\,d\nu} {Z_{F,+}^{\rm end}} \le \exp\left(\sum_\ell d_\ell e^{2s_\ell}\right)-1. \label{eq:comparison-flat-cover}$$ The constants are independent of the cutoff depth, the periods, their aspect ratio, and $P$. The estimate also bounds the absolute difference of the two integrals after insertion of any common measurable multiplier of modulus at most one.
  - Explanation: Bounds the integrated absolute difference of mandatory covers by their weighted label discrepancies, including complex comparison weights and bounded common multipliers.
- **claim-nearby-fugacity-pressure-control** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-comparison-nearby-fugacity)): Fix the blocking factor $L$ and the admission constants as above. Let $(b,r)$ be the matched Brownian parameters supplied by <a href="#eq:R15" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:R15">[eq:R15]</a>, with $b=\beta+O_L(1)$ and $r=1+O_L(1/b)$. Consider the periodic rectangle with initial side lengths $$X=L^N m_x,\qquad n=L^N m_t,\qquad m_x\asymp\beta(\log\beta)^2,\qquad m_t\asymp\sqrt\beta(\log\beta)^4,$$ where the terminal lengths are dyadic and satisfy the admission conditions. Write $V=m_xm_t$ and $V_{\mathrm{site}}=Xn=L^{2N}V$. For $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}$ set $$b'=b\exp\!\left(\frac{\sigma}{2b}\right),\qquad r'=r\frac{b'}b.$$ Thus the fugacity $\lambda_{\mathrm{fug}}=b^2/2$ changes by $\log(\lambda_{\mathrm{fug}}'/\lambda_{\mathrm{fug}})=\sigma/b$, while $r'/b'=r/b$. In particular, the horizontal heat time per initial interval, the width $W=Xr/b$, and the rectangle volume are unchanged. For all sufficiently large $\beta$, the actual untwisted Brownian partition functions satisfy $$\log Z^B(b',r')-\log Z^B(b,r) \le V_{\mathrm{site}} \left[b'r'-br+O_L\!\left(\frac1b\right)\right]. \label{eq:R17}$$ The error is uniform in $\sigma$ and in the indicated rectangle lengths, with fixed constants in the two $\asymp$ conditions; the assertion also holds with $m_t$ replaced by $2m_t$.
  - Explanation: Bounds pressure changes under the specified fugacity perturbations while fixing horizontal heat time, width, and volume.
- **claim-ordered-limit-helicity-matching** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-matching-helicity)): Fix the blocking factor $L$ and the admission constants as in Sections <a href="#sec:rg" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:rg">7</a>–<a href="#sec:comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:comparison">9</a>. For every sufficiently large $\beta$, choose any matched trajectory satisfying <a href="#eq:R15" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:R15">[eq:R15]</a>, with its parameters $b,r,c_x,c_t$. For $i=x,t$, $$\lim_{m\to\infty}\limsup_{s\to\infty}\limsup_{\beta\to\infty} \left\|h_i^B(mL^s)-h_i^F(mL^s)\right\|=0, \label{eq:R18}$$ where $m$ tends to infinity through sufficiently large dyadic integers. The inner limit is taken with $m$ and $s$ fixed.
  - Explanation: Matches the constant-order helicity responses through fixed-volume expansions with the stated order of limits.
- **claim-microscopic-gaussian-helicities** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-matching-microscopic-helicity)): For each fixed even $n$, along the matched parameters as $\beta\to\infty$, $$h_i^F(n)=\beta-\frac32\int_{W,n}\frac{D_i}{D} -4\int_{W,n}\frac{\sin^2 k_i}{D^2}+o(1), \qquad i=x,t, \label{eq:R19}$$ and $$\begin{aligned} h_x^B(n)&=\frac br-4\int_{B,n}\frac{k_x^2}{D_*^2}+o(1),\\ h_t^B(n)&=br-2\int_{B,n}\frac{D_t}{D_*} -4\int_{B,n}\frac{\sin^2 k_t-D_t^2/4}{D_*^2}+o(1). \end{aligned} \label{eq:R20}$$ The errors tend to zero with $n$ fixed. In the correction terms the shape parameter has already been replaced by its limit $r=1$.
  - Explanation: Computes the directional microscopic helicities, including the bilinear current correction from the complex Brownian weight.
- **claim-finite-matched-coupling-shift** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-matching-coupling-shift)): For every choice of matched parameters satisfying <a href="#eq:R15" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:R15">[eq:R15]</a>, $$\beta-b=\frac14-\frac{1+\log 2}{2\pi}+o(1) \qquad (\beta\to\infty). \label{eq:R21}$$
  - Explanation: Determines the additive coupling shift that changes the leading lattice mass prefactor.
- **claim-wilson-parity-trace-asymptotics** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-assembly-wilson-traces)): For the rectangles <a href="#eq:assembly-rectangles" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:assembly-rectangles">[eq:assembly-rectangles]</a>, uniformly along the matched trajectories, $$\log\frac{Z_1^q(t)}{Z_0^q(t)} =-\frac{t}{a}m_{\rm lat}(\beta)+o(t), \qquad 2\log Z_0^q(t)-\log Z_0^q(2t)=o(1). \label{eq:C1}$$ The first formula also holds with $t$ replaced by $2t$.
  - Explanation: Extracts the full lattice mass from the odd-to-even Wilson trace ratio and controls the even trace under time doubling.
- **claim-extra-circle-removal** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-assembly-circle)): For $l=0,1$, at both time lengths $t$ and $2t$, $$Z_l^{F(\phi)}(t)=Z_G(t)Z_l^q(t)(1+o(1)). \label{eq:C2}$$ Moreover, $$2\log Z_G(t)-\log Z_G(2t)=o(t). \label{eq:C3}$$
  - Explanation: Factors out the zero-winding Gaussian circle contribution and shows that its time-doubling remainder is negligible on the mass-extraction scale.
- **claim-positive-operator-trace-doubling** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-assembly-trace-norm)): Let $A$ be a nonzero positive compact operator. Suppose $A^n$ is trace class for a positive integer $n$, and write $\tau=\\|A\\|$. Then $$0\le\log\frac{\operatorname{Tr}A^n}{\tau^n} \le 2\log\operatorname{Tr}A^n-\log\operatorname{Tr}A^{2n}.$$ The same conclusion holds for a direct sum of positive operators whenever the indicated total trace is finite.
  - Explanation: Bounds the logarithmic excess of a positive operator trace over the norm power by its trace-doubling defect.
- **claim-maximizing-particle-density** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-assembly-particle-density)): For either parity, every particle number $j$ attaining $\tau_l$ on the width <a href="#eq:assembly-rectangles" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:assembly-rectangles">[eq:assembly-rectangles]</a> satisfies $$\frac jW=b^2+O(b),$$ with a constant uniform as $\beta\to\infty$.
  - Explanation: Verifies the density band required by the Brownian parity theorem for every maximizing sector of both parities.

        "anchor": "stmt-brownian-halfline",
        "exact_quote": "There are functions $U,V:[0,\\infty)\\to\\mathbb R$, continuous from the right at zero and continuous on $(0,\\infty)$, with the following properties. Extend $U$ by zero on $(-\\infty,0)$. Then $$U(X)=(K_1*U)(X)\\quad(X>0),\n \\qquad V(Y)=(K_1*U)(-Y)\\quad(Y\\ge0),$$ and $U(X)>0$, $V(Y)>0$ for $X,Y\\ge0$. For $\\operatorname{Re}s>0$, $$\\label{eq:B7}\n\\begin{split}\n C(s)&=\\frac{\\sqrt{s}\\,\n  \\exp\\!\\left\\{\\frac{s}{2\\pi}\n             \\left(\\log\\frac{s}{2\\pi}-1\\right)\\right\\}}\n {\\Gamma(1+s/(2\\pi))},\\\\\n \\int_0^\\infty e^{-sX}U(X)\\,dX\n   &=\\frac{\\sqrt\\pi}{2sC(s)},\\qquad\n \\int_0^\\infty e^{-sY}V(Y)\\,dY\n   =\\frac{\\sqrt\\pi}{2s}C(s).\n\\end{split}$$ The logarithm and square root in this formula are the principal branches. Moreover, $$\\label{brownian:U-asymptotic}\n\\begin{aligned}\n U(X)&=\\sqrt X+\n       \\frac{\\log X+C'}{4\\pi\\sqrt X}\n       +O\\!\\left(X^{-3/2}(1+\\log^2X)\\right),\\\\\n C'&=\\log(8\\pi)+1,\\qquad X\\longrightarrow\\infty,\n\\end{aligned}$$ while $V(Y)=O((1+Y)^{-1/2})$ and $U(0)=V(0)=\\sqrt\\pi/2$.",
        "source_id": "PM-215.3"
      },

For $\\operatorname{Re}s>0$, $$\\label{eq:B7}\n\\begin{split}\n C(s)&=\\frac{\\sqrt{s}\\,\n  \\exp\\!\\left\\{\\frac{s}{2\\pi}\n             \\left(\\log\\frac{s}{2\\pi}-1\\right)\\right\\}}\n {\\Gamma(1+s/(2\\pi))},\\\\\n \\int_0^\\infty e^{-sX}U(X)\\,dX\n   &=\\frac{\\sqrt\\pi}{2sC(s)},\\qquad\n \\int_0^\\infty e^{-sY}V(Y)\\,dY\n   =\\frac{\\sqrt\\pi}{2s}C(s).\n\\end{split}$$ The logarithm and square root in this formula are the principal branches.         "exact_quote": "Suppose the momenta and auxiliary variables are nonsingular solutions of $$\\label{eq:B8}\n \\begin{aligned}\n e^{ik_j\\mathcal W}\n   &=e^{i\\zeta+2i\\chi}\n       \\prod_{t\\ne j}\\frac{k_j-k_t+2i}{k_j-k_t-2i}\n       \\left(\\frac{Q_0(k_j-i)}{Q_0(k_j+i)}\\right)^2,\n       &&1\\leq j\\leq n_p,\\\\\n e^{-2i\\chi}\\prod_{j=1}^{n_p}\n       \\frac{a_r-k_j-i}{a_r-k_j+i}\n   &=\\prod_{s\\ne r}\\frac{a_r-a_s-2i}{a_r-a_s+2i},\n       &&1\\leq r\\leq M.\n \\end{aligned}$$ Here nonsingular means that the displayed rational functions and the coefficient formulas in the proof are defined by ordinary substitution. For each binary index, apply the upper-right entries $B(a_1),\\ldots,B(a_M)$ of the spin-$\\frac12$ monodromy defined below to the all-up vector.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-bethe-line",
        "exact_quote": "For every fixed integer $n_p=2M+\\ell\\geq0$, every $c>0$, and every $s>0$, the heat kernel of $H_c$ on the ordered line chamber is $$\\begin{split}\n e^{-sH_c}(X,Y)\n  ={}&\\sum_{\\ell'+2m'=n_p}\n       \\frac{(2c)^{m'}}{\\ell'!\\,m'!}\n       \\int_{\\mathbb R^{\\ell'+m'}}\n       E_X^{\\ell'm'}(k,u)E_Y^{\\ell'm'}(k,u)^\\dagger\\\\\n    &\\quad{}\\times\n       \\exp\\left\\{-s\\left(\n           \\sum_{a=1}^{\\ell'}k_a^2+\n           2\\sum_{a=1}^{m'}u_a^2-\\frac{m'c^2}{2}\n                    \\right)\\right\\}\n       \\prod_{a=1}^{\\ell'}\\frac{dk_a}{2\\pi}\n       \\prod_{a=1}^{m'}\\frac{du_a}{2\\pi}.\n\\end{split}\n\\label{eq:B10}$$ Empty products and the vacuum term have their usual value $1$. The transform defined by the kernels in <a href=\"#eq:B10\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:B10\">[eq:B10]</a>, with the square roots of the displayed weights, is an isometry. Moreover, $H_c+Mc^2/2\\geq0$, and its quadratic form is the integral of $$\\sum_{a=1}^{\\ell'}k_a^2+\n  2\\sum_{a=1}^{m'}u_a^2+\\frac{(M-m')c^2}{2}$$ against the squared modulus of this transform.",
        "source_id": "PM-215.3"
      },

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-bethe-pair-compactness",
        "exact_quote": "Fix $W_0>0$, $n_p=2M+\\ell$, and $C<\\infty$. For each seam and pair assignment these limits are compatible under enlargement of the chart and have the form $$f_{\\alpha,\\mathfrak p}(q,v)\\,\n \\exp\\left\\{-\\frac12\\sum_{a=1}^M z_a\\right\\}\n \\bigotimes_{a=1}^M\n        (s_a^L\\otimes s_a^R).\n\\label{eq:B12}$$ Here $v$ and its color are present only if $\\ell=1$; the coefficient $f_{\\alpha,\\mathfrak p}$ includes that color. As $\\delta\\downarrow0$ and $Z\\uparrow\\infty$, the sum of the squared norms of these chart limits tends to $1$, counted with the fixed square partition of unity. There is no norm lost away from the pair coincidence manifolds or at their intersections. Inner products of two sequences converging in this sense converge to the corresponding sums of inner products of their limits.",

        "anchor": "stmt-cor-bethe-ground-test",
        "exact_quote": "Fix a circle length $W_0>0$ and a particle number $n_p=2M+\\ell$, with $\\ell\\in\\{0,1\\}$, and work in the fixed-weight sector balanced in each binary index.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-bethe-centers",
        "exact_quote": "Under the parameter assumptions at the start of this Section, for every $\\mathcal W\\geq W$, <a href=\"#eq:B13\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:B13\">[eq:B13]</a> has a reflection-symmetric solution with $v=0$ and $u_1<\\cdots<u_M$. With $v$ fixed, the pair solution is unique. Define $$Z_c(x)=\\frac{x}{\\pi}\n    +\\frac{1}{\\pi\\mathcal W}\\sum_{j=1}^M\n           \\arctan\\frac{x-u_j}{4}\n    -\\frac{\\ell}{2\\pi\\mathcal W}\\varphi(x),\n \\qquad d(x)=Z_c'(x).$$ Then $Z_c$ is odd and $$d(x)=\\frac1\\pi+\\frac1{\\mathcal W}\\sum_jK(x-u_j)\n             -\\frac\\ell{\\mathcal W}(K_1-K_3)(x),\n \\qquad\n Z_c(u_j)=\\frac{j-(M+1)/2}{\\mathcal W}.$$ Let $B_c>0$ be determined by $Z_c(B_c)=M/(2\\mathcal W)$. The following bounds hold uniformly:*\n\n1.  *$d$ is bounded below by a positive constant; $B_c=O((1+b)^2)$; $d$ and any fixed number of its derivatives are bounded by $\\operatorname{poly}(b)$. Neighboring centers have separation at least $1/(\\mathcal W\\operatorname{poly}(b))$.*\n\n\n2.  *On $(-B_c,B_c)$, $$\\label{eq:B14}\n     d=\\rho_{B_c}\n      -\\frac\\ell{\\mathcal W}(1-K*)_{B_c}^{-1}(K_1-K_3)\n      +O\\!\\left(\\frac{\\operatorname{poly}(b)}{\\mathcal W^2}\\right).$$ The inverse function in the middle term has bounded supremum and $L^1$ norm, independently of $B_c$.*\n\n3.  *$B_c\\leq B_*+O(1)$. At $\\mathcal W=W$ one also has $B_c\\geq B_*-O(1)$.*\n\n4.  *The full Jacobian of <a href=\"#eq:B13\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:B13\">[eq:B13]</a>, including the single equation when present, is invertible. Its inverse has row sums bounded by a fixed power of $\\mathcal W$.",
        "source_id": "PM-215.3"
      },

        "exact_quote": "Let the centers be those of Lemma <a href=\"#lem:bethe-centers\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:bethe-centers\">21</a>.         "exact_quote": "For the parameter range of this Section, the center solution of <a href=\"#eq:B13\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:B13\">[eq:B13]</a> has a locally unique continuation to solutions of <a href=\"#eq:B8\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:B8\">[eq:B8]</a>, with the singular solutions understood as analytic continuation limits. At zero twist write these solutions as $$k_{j+}=a_j+i+X_j,\\qquad k_{j-}=a_j-i+Y_j,\n \\qquad u_j^{\\mathrm{true}}=(k_{j+}+k_{j-})/2.$$ For every fixed $A_0>0$, the differences between the true variables and their formal center values are $O_{A_0}(\\mathcal W^{-A_0})$, uniformly for $\\mathcal W\\geq W$, once $b$ is sufficiently large. The solutions are locally analytic in $\\mathcal W$ and in twists near zero, and these local solutions link along $[W,\\infty)$. At fixed $n_p$, their zero-twist centers satisfy $$\\label{eq:B18}\n u_j=\\frac{\\pi(j-(M+1)/2)}{\\mathcal W}\n             +O_{n_p}(\\mathcal W^{-2})\n       \\qquad (\\mathcal W\\to\\infty).$$ Ordinary nonsingular parameters form a generic set on this continued branch. A common twist translates every rapidity by $\\zeta/\\mathcal W$.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-rg-free",
        "exact_quote": "For either initial precision and either admissible shape, the free block iteration has uniformly elliptic, exponentially localized precisions $K_h$, conditional means $\\mathsf P_h$, conditional covariances $C_h$, and positive edge stacks. Their required fixed derivatives, including shape derivatives, obey bounds on one common complex momentum neighborhood. For two initial precisions with the same shape, their histories differ by $CL^{-h}$ in those bounds. Constants needed to choose $L$ are independent of sufficiently large $L$.*\n\n\n*For a Brownian strip the edge lift consists of the horizontal term $l^{-1}$ and a positive matrix on the two endpoint values of each vertical edge. If $z$ is the vertical edge Laplacian symbol, this matrix is $$B_l(z)=l\\sum_{m\\ge1}J_m^*\n          \\bigl(1+l^2z/(\\pi m)^2\\bigr)^{-1}J_m,\n \\qquad J_s(c,c')=(1-s)c+sc',\n \\label{eq:R3}$$ where $J_m$ is the $m$th normalized sine coefficient of $J_s$. It is analytic near $[0,4]$, with uniform positive lower and upper bounds on that real interval. The formula holds also for cut vertical arrays, using their existing bonds. The affine precision, after strips are summed, is $\\operatorname{diag}(l^{-1},l)$.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-rg-joint",
        "exact_quote": "Fix a primary pattern and the complete-support convention above. Form local factors from: nonlinear rows minus their affine squares; stationary squares; old polynomial and regular-error terms; exceptional numerical defects; determinant and Gaussian-ratio chains; Haar Jacobian ratios; opened default-profile failures; and old covering weights. Include the compulsory cores and their frozen integrations.*\n\n*Suppose their ordinary smooth factors have envelopes $C_Lg^r\\operatorname{poly}(M_j,p_j,s)$ of positive order $r$; ratio exponents have bounds $$|Q_\\alpha(Z)|\\le e_\\alpha\n        \\left(1+\\sum_{x\\in I_\\alpha}|Z_x|^2\\right);$$ their eighth-root support-hit sums are sufficiently small; and every selection of $n$ distinct failure tests has simultaneous probability at most $\\exp(-c_Lp_j^2n/M_j^D)$. Suppose further that the frozen integral of each core satisfies $$\\int|B_c|\\le\\exp\\{-c_Lp_j^2s_c+\n C_LM_j^D(1+|\\log g|)s_c\\}$$ uniformly in the Gaussian arguments, while retaining the output-flag and curvature reserves. Here $B_c$ is the core integrand; its integral includes the frozen quaternion and real variables and the residual integer and tag sums, with Gaussian and output arguments held fixed. Suppose also that differentiation through hard dependencies can be represented by one simultaneous transport whose fixed-order $L^4$ scores cost a polynomial in total load and a fixed power of $g^{-1}$. Whenever such a negative power occurs, retain a core, failure, or exponentially accurate factor to pay it. Assume explicitly that every allowed differentiated product is a sum of polynomially many terms retaining the ordinary and ratio envelopes and the closed failure supports, apart from these score factors; a marked discrepancy uses its replacement envelope.*\n\n*Then every finite selection has a joint integral bound equal to the product of its stated majorants times a fixed polynomial in total load. This holds through eight normalized output derivatives for empty output inventory, and through seven derivatives for one marked input or parameter discrepancy. With nonempty output inventory it gives the sup norm and the corresponding discrepancy bound. A core with $s_c$ seeds retains $e^{-c_Lp_j^2s_c}$ after fixed losses, and each failure test retains $e^{-c_Lp_j^2/M_j^D}$; ratio chains may use their eighth-root envelopes. Disjoint complete supports factor exactly; overlapping factors require no independence.",

        "exact_quote": "The principal Taylor map through normalized order four produces exactly the slots <a href=\"#eq:R5\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:R5\">[eq:R5]</a>, scalar terms, an imaginary temporal linear $w$ term, and the four affine kinetic corrections in <a href=\"#eq:R6\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:R6\">[eq:R6]</a>.         "anchor": "stmt-prop-init-density",
        "exact_quote": "For the parameter choices of Theorem <a href=\"#thm:rg-step\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"thm:rg-step\">32</a>, the flat Wilson reference and the Brownian strip integral have exact representations in the retained class at scale $N$, on every admitted rectangle and with either time seam. The Wilson reference starts with zero canonical and regular-error lists and with flat covering labels. The Brownian representation starts from the uncorrected affine couplings $$(B_x^q,B_t^q)=b(r^{-1},r),\\qquad\n (B_x^w,B_t^w)=bR^{-2}(r^{-1},r).$$ Its actual affine couplings differ from these by at most $C_L$. Their corrections, and its initial canonical coefficients, are given by the finite Taylor calculation through normalized order four, with coupling error $O_L(H_N^{-1.05})$. Its canonical caps can be fixed before choosing $P_0$ and $H$. All assertions include the normalized derivatives and period prescriptions of the retained class. The scalar extracted per initial site is the quantity in <a href=\"#eq:R14\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:R14\">[eq:R14]</a> below.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-init-completion",
        "exact_quote": "For a finite periodic regular-row array or an array with arbitrary deleted rows, the Gaussian completion of <a href=\"#eq:R13\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:R13\">[eq:R13]</a> admits finite-range numerical means and covariances. The covariances have uniform positive upper and lower bounds. The means and covariance deviations from the identity have exponential position bounds and summable estimates over bridge modes. Their exact Gaussian ratio factors satisfy the joint moment and support estimates used in Lemma <a href=\"#lem:rg-joint\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:rg-joint\">34</a>. The stationary energy is the strip energy <a href=\"#eq:R3\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:R3\">[eq:R3]</a>, up to local errors $C\\operatorname{poly}(M,p)e^{-c_LM}$ in chart norms.           "exact_quote": "For a finite periodic regular-row array or an array with arbitrary deleted rows, the Gaussian completion of <a href=\"#eq:R13\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:R13\">[eq:R13]</a> admits finite-range numerical means and covariances. The stationary energy is the strip energy <a href=\"#eq:R3\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:R3\">[eq:R3]</a>, up to local errors $C\\operatorname{poly}(M,p)e^{-c_LM}$ in chart norms. Let $\\widetilde\\Xi^\\eta$ be another mandatory covering sum with the same inventory conventions and complete supports, allowing complex weights. Use a common label list, setting absent weights equal to zero, and define $$d_\\ell=\\|\\widetilde\\kappa_\\ell-\\kappa_{\\ell,F}\\|_\\infty,\n \\qquad\n b_\\ell=\\|\\widetilde\\kappa_\\ell\\|_\\infty+\n              \\|\\kappa_{\\ell,F}\\|_\\infty.$$ Suppose $$\\sup_x\\sum_{\\ell:x\\in P_\\ell}e^{64s_\\ell}b_\\ell\n \\le C\\exp(-p_0^{1/4}),$$ with the fixed multiplier $C$, and with the support and load bounds of the retained class. Then, for either $\\eta$, $$\\frac{\\displaystyle\\int_{\\mathcal F}e^{X_F^\\eta}\n              |\\widetilde\\Xi^\\eta-\\Xi_F^\\eta|\\,d\\nu}\n      {Z_{F,+}^{\\rm end}}\n \\le\n \\exp\\left(\\sum_\\ell d_\\ell e^{2s_\\ell}\\right)-1.\n \\label{eq:comparison-flat-cover}$$ The constants are independent of the cutoff depth, the periods, their aspect ratio, and $P$. Write $V=m_xm_t$ and $V_{\\mathrm{site}}=Xn=L^{2N}V$. For $\\sigma\\in\\{-1,1\\}$ set $$b'=b\\exp\\!\\left(\\frac{\\sigma}{2b}\\right),\\qquad\n  r'=r\\frac{b'}b.$$ Thus the fugacity $\\lambda_{\\mathrm{fug}}=b^2/2$ changes by $\\log(\\lambda_{\\mathrm{fug}}'/\\lambda_{\\mathrm{fug}})=\\sigma/b$, while $r'/b'=r/b$. <a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Associated law** ([source](#eq:wilson-two-planes)): A law of real variables is *associated* if any two bounded coordinatewise increasing functions have nonnegative covariance.
- **Spin monomial and site list** ([source](#sec:sector)): Here a monomial is a product of individual spin components with coefficient one. Its site list has one entry for each factor, including repetitions.
- **Observable inversion parity** ([source](#pm-h-10)): An observable is *even* or *odd* according to its parity under simultaneous inversion $q_x\mapsto-q_x$ at every site.
- **Component reflection** ([source](#pm-h-10)): A *component reflection* reverses one fixed component at every site and leaves the others unchanged.
- **Admitted nearest-neighbor trajectory** ([source](#pm-h-12)): An *admitted nearest-neighbor trajectory of depth $N$* is the exact $N$-step block integration of the nearest-neighbor Wilson law constructed in (**SharpO4?** and 7.1).
- **Balanced fixed-weight sector** ([source](#pm-h-18)): The *balanced sector* has $\lfloor n_{\mathrm p}/2\rfloor$ such occurrences in each index.
- **Dressed energy** ([source](#eq:B3)): We call $\epsilon$ the dressed energy.
- **Retained density** ([source](#stmt-def-rg-retained-class)): A retained density is an expression $$\exp\!\left\{i\theta\sum_{e_t}u_e\right\} \exp\{V\|\Lambda\|-B\mathcal E-X_{\rm can}-X_{\rm err}\}\,\Xi, \label{eq:R2}$$ with the four kinetic coefficients in the bands above and the numerical energy $\mathcal E$ formed from the direct terms <a href="#eq:R4" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:R4">[eq:R4]</a> and the enabled second-stack squares. If $\mathcal P_a$ denotes a canonical label, including its displayed prefactor in <a href="#eq:R5" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:R5">[eq:R5]</a>, write $$X_{\rm can}=\sum_a1_{X_a}\mathcal P_a, \qquad X_{\rm err}=\sum_X1_Xf_X.$$ Here $X_a$ is the declared graph of the complete polynomial label, including its compensators and paths. Each masked term is defined to be zero outside its graph domain, so no local continuation is evaluated there. The errors and covering sum have the stated norms. Each polynomial slot has a fixed coefficient cap, chosen successively in its displayed order. The real number $\theta$ is unrestricted. Bulk scalars and coefficient extractions are independent of the periods and seam. All terms obey the listed symmetries, with orbit assignments made on complete labels. Reference covering weights vanish whenever a plaquette containing an edge of their inventory is nonflat. Brownian weights restricted to the condition that some such plaquette is nonflat obey their covering cap with the additional factor $e^{-F_h}$, where $F_0=0$. These plaquette tests belong to the complete support.
- **Nonwinding record** ([source](#eq:rg-load-projection)): A record is *nonwinding* if its load is less than a fixed small constant times the short period divided by $M_j$; its lift is then injective and its formula is the bulk formula.
- **Medoid observation target** ([source](#pm-h-37)): Such a minimizing constituent is called a medoid.
- **Regular strip rows** ([source](#pm-h-48)): The rows not deleted in a given term are called *regular rows*.

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-angular-signs** [claim](#stmt-lem-wilson-signs) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-wilson-signs): Conditional rotators, mixed derivatives, and association. -> Angular association and component covariance signs.
- **step-sector-covariance** [claim](#stmt-prop-wilson-covariance) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-wilson-covariance): Positive pairing expansion and conditional covariance decomposition. -> Parity-dependent monomial covariance bounds.
- **step-full-gap** [claim](#stmt-prop-wilson-full-gap) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-wilson-full-gap): Positive spectral measures and polynomial density in the reconstructed space. -> Spin detection of the full gap and the centered even-sector bound.
- **step-cylinder-detector** [claim](#stmt-lem-wilson-detector) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-wilson-detector): Even-sector spectral bound and the sign of an excited eigenfunction. -> Bounded component-odd detector with a lower overlap bound.
- **step-cylinder-visibility** [claim](#stmt-lem-wilson-visibility) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-wilson-visibility): Conditional sign clusters and amplitude comparison. -> Detector correlations bounded by component pair correlations.
- **step-wilson-input** [claim](#stmt-prop-wilson-input) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-wilson-input): Import trajectory, calibration, seed, and full-gap results with matching conventions. -> Uniform admitted-trajectory input.
- **step-long-rectangles** [claim](#stmt-lem-wilson-long-rectangles) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-wilson-long-rectangles): Iterate exact rectangle identities and advance trace tails. -> Long-rectangle trace-defect estimate.
- **step-cylinder-partition-rate** [claim](#stmt-prop-wilson-partition-rate) / [proof](#pm-h-14): Converge capped cylinder rates, identify their plane limit, and remove the cap. -> Uniform cylinder and partition rates.
- **step-contact-ground** [claim](#stmt-lem-brownian-ground) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-brownian-ground): Cooperative contact forms, positivity improvement, and weak-form commutation. -> Simple positive balanced ground state attaining the transfer norm.
- **step-endpoint-equations** [claim](#stmt-lem-brownian-equations) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-brownian-equations): Positive Neumann resolvent and monotonicity of the odd integral equation. -> Unique density, selected coupling, and dressed-energy sign.
- **step-halfline-profile** [claim](#stmt-brownian-halfline) / [proof](#proof-stmt-brownian-halfline): Laplace inversion and Wiener–Hopf factorization with a positivity argument. -> Positive endpoint profiles and their asymptotic correction.
- **step-uniform-matching** [claim](#stmt-brownian-uniform) / [proof](#proof-stmt-brownian-uniform): Cancel endpoint singularities and compare the residual with kernel mass loss. -> Uniform composite endpoint approximation.
- **step-endpoint-asymptotics** [claim](#stmt-prop-brownian-asymptotics) / [proof](#pm-h-23): Integrate the matched density and exterior profile with dominated convergence. -> Endpoint, density, and odd-mass asymptotics.
- **step-bethe-algebra** [claim](#stmt-lem-bethe-algebra) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-bethe-algebra): Monodromy commutation, fusion, and periodic transport. -> Twisted eigenfunctions and auxiliary trace eigenvalues.
- **step-line-resolution** [claim](#stmt-lem-bethe-line) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-bethe-line): Separated heat contours, residue cancellation, and isometric reconstruction. -> Line spectral resolution and shifted energy form.
- **step-shuffle-decay** [claim](#stmt-lem-bethe-shuffle-decay) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-bethe-shuffle-decay): Group removable poles and apply uniform Cauchy estimates. -> Exponential decay across pair spans.
- **step-pair-compactness** [claim](#stmt-lem-bethe-pair-compactness) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-bethe-pair-compactness): Localize at seams, truncate spectral momenta, and exhaust separated pair charts. -> Strong chart compactness without norm loss.
- **step-positive-overlap-test** [claim](#stmt-cor-bethe-ground-test) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-bethe-ground-test): Compare positive limiting overlaps with spectral orthogonality. -> Strong-coupling ground-branch test.
- **step-center-equations** [claim](#stmt-lem-bethe-centers) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-bethe-centers): Convex minimization, quantile midpoint summation, and Schur-complement control. -> Ordered centers, counting density, and invertible Jacobian.
- **step-spacing-suppression** [claim](#stmt-lem-bethe-suppression) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-bethe-suppression): Positive convolution representation and logarithmic quadrature estimates. -> Uniform suppression of pair-spacing corrections.
- **step-root-continuation** [claim](#stmt-lem-bethe-roots) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-bethe-roots): Regularize internal pair factors and contract a Newton correction map. -> Linked analytic finite-circle root branch.
- **step-ground-branch** [claim](#stmt-prop-bethe-ground) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-bethe-ground): Evaluate the strong-coupling center wave and continue a simple eigenlevel. -> Identification of the branch with the balanced ground state.
- **step-transfer-formula** [claim](#stmt-lem-bethe-transfer-formula) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-bethe-transfer-formula): Extract plane coefficients in the heat-loop rotor expansion. -> Exact finite-circle transfer scalar with all rotor sectors.
- **step-uniform-transfer** [claim](#stmt-lem-bethe-transfer-uniform) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-bethe-transfer-uniform): Bound fused pair factors and remove singular single factors by analyticity. -> Uniform leading transfer product and rotor suppression.
- **step-parity-quadrature** [claim](#stmt-lem-bethe-parity-error) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-bethe-parity-error): Midpoint expansion in the counting coordinate and endpoint adjustment. -> Uniform variational bracket bounds and near-optimal particle counts.
